title: Priority Regulator: token-econ and SLA tradeoffs
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: PM needs a deterministic, auditable way to rank roadmap candidates that balances impact, effort, reach (RICE) with per-token cost and SLA exposure for inference workloads. Current RICE-only approaches underweight sustained token costs and the downstream impact of latency SLO violations.

Proposal summary: Implement a "Priority Regulator"—a RICE-derived scoring formula augmented with two penalty terms: a token-econ delta (expected incremental $/1M tokens over 90 days) and an SLA-exposure multiplier (probability-weighted cost of latency regressions). The regulator yields a single score for ranking and supports scenario simulation for capacity regimes (normal, constrained, burst).
proposed_solution:
1) Extend RICE to RICE+: Score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort - TokenPenalty * CapacityFactor - SLA_Multiplier.
2) TokenPenalty = expected_delta_cost_per_1M_tokens / cost_normalizer.
3) SLA_Multiplier = SLA_risk_prob * SLA_penalty_scale (derived from historical incident costs).
4) CapacityFactor: maps forecasted utilization (0-1) to an amplification of TokenPenalty during constrained regimes.
5) Ship as a small web tool in Console (prioritizer tab) and a CSV export for PMs; make algorithm auditable with parameter knobs and versioned release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Calculator implemented in Console with editable knobs for TokenPenalty, SLA_penalty_scale, and CapacityFactor
Documentation (Confluence) that explains math, assumptions, and example calculations
Backend service returns deterministic score for a given candidate and param set; endpoint documented in API spec
Smoke test demonstrating scores change sensibly under a simulated token-cost doubling and an SLA risk increase
Stakeholder signoff (PM, Eng, Finance) on default parameter values
sample_calculation: Example candidate A: Reach=200k users, Impact=0.3 (0.0-1.0), Confidence=0.7, Effort=8 points. Base RICE = (200k * 0.3 * 0.7)/8 = 5,250. Expected token delta = $150 per 1M tokens -> TokenPenalty normalized = 150/100 = 1.5. CapacityFactor (normal)=1.0, SLA_risk_prob=0.02, SLA_penalty_scale=200 -> SLA_Multiplier = 4. Score = 5250 - 1.5*1 - 4 = 5244.5. Under constrained (CapacityFactor=3) Token penalty contribution = 4.5, Score=5241.5 (rank changes only for low-base RICE items).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): design doc, parameter defaults with Finance, simple web prototype (PM Console mock). Phase 2 (3 weeks): backend API, audit logs, CSV export; internal beta with three PM teams. Phase 3 (2 weeks): adjust params from beta feedback, add scenario simulation, enable for roadmap planning cycles. Post-launch: quarterly review of penalty scalars tied to infra cost reports.
metrics: Adoption: # of PMs using Priority Regulator in cycle planning (target 60% of roadmap PMs by next cycle)
Rank stability: % of top-10 ranked items preserved when toggling CapacityFactor between normal and constrained (target >70%)
Prediction alignment: correlation between predicted token delta and actual delta (target Pearson r>0.6 after 90 days)
SLA incident reduction: trend of features ranked to reduce SLA exposure (qualitative tracking)
Time saved: average minutes saved in prioritization meetings (survey-based)
decisions: Adopt RICE+ formula (RICE with subtractive token penalty and SLA multiplier) rather than multiplicative reweighting to preserve base RICE signal
Normalize token penalty by an internal cost_normalizer (100 $/1M tokens) to keep scores on a human-readable scale
Expose knobs to PMs but keep Finance-approved defaults in product config
CapacityFactor will be a piecewise linear function with breakpoints at 0.6 and 0.85 utilization
tradeoffs: Pros: More economically aware prioritization leads to fewer high-cost low-value launches; supports capacity-aware roadmaps
Cons: Introduces forecast dependencies (token usage estimates) which increase noise; risk of gaming by teams submitting optimistic reach/impact
Mitigations: require provenance links for usage forecasts and a lightweight validation checklist reviewed by Solutions Eng
open_questions: What is the canonical source for expected token deltas? (Estimator in analytics or ask owning team?)
How often should defaults be re-evaluated against infra run-rate (quarterly vs monthly)?
Should we include an explicit privacy/compliance multiplier for Private deployments (higher penalty when customer-managed infra costs are non-linear)?
